title: Jet-Long: Efficient Long-Context Extension with Dynamic Bifocal RoPE
claim: Fixed-factor extension methods degrade sharply as context grows, while ours stays best at every length and keeps base-model quality at short lengths.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis, bottom legend, off-chart values marked with triangles
description: Two line plots sit side by side and share a log-spaced x-axis of context length, from 4096 to 131072, labeled once below. The left plot shows RULER accuracy falling from about 90 to 40 as context grows. The right plot shows PG-19 perplexity between about 11 and 14. Six methods are drawn as lines with dots: Qwen3 1.7B Base (gray), +DNTK (purple), +YaRN (red), +DCA (blue), +Self-extend (orange) and +Jet-Long (ours). The Jet-Long line is thick and saturated green, and the baselines are thin and faded. In the left plot, the baselines fall away at long context, and gray drops off the bottom. In the right plot, baseline perplexity shoots off the top. Triangles at the top edge mark these points, with their values printed below, such as 22.3, 71.0 and 14.4. The eye goes first to the green line, which stays highest in accuracy and lowest in perplexity. A shared legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Qwen3-1.7B-Base RULER accuracy, averaged over all 13 tasks, and PG-19 perplexity at the six main context lengths. Jet-Long improves extended-context performance while preserving the base attention rule within the native window. The revised H100 efficiency comparison, with FA3 as the primary reference and a matched CuTe control, is reported in Section [ref].
abstract: Modern LLMs are increasingly deployed in long-context applications such as retrieval-augmented generation, repository-level coding, and agentic workflows whose accumulated reasoning and tool traces routinely push the input an order of magnitude past the pretraining window, making zero-shot context extension the dominant deployment path for open-weight checkpoints. The dominant zero-shot methods (YaRN, Self-Extend, DCA) fix a single rescaling factor up front, so an aggressive factor sacrifices short-context fidelity while a conservative one breaks down at long contexts; recent length-aware variants adapt the mapping, but with a fitted or distance-dependent schedule. We propose Jet-Long, a tuning-free zero-shot method that pairs a local RoPE-faithful window with a long-range window whose rescaling factor adapts dynamically to the current sequence length via a parameter-free analytic schedule, recovering the base model exactly at short inputs while extrapolating cleanly at long ones. An inclusion-exclusion attention merge and on-the-fly RoPE correction enable a fused CuTe implementation. On H100 at 64K-128K, prefill retains 83-88% of FlashAttention-3 throughput across the evaluated Qwen3 sizes and 88-93% of a matched CuTe control; Qwen3-8B single-batch generation reaches 1.04-1.08 times FlashAttention-3 throughput. On Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B up to 128K context, Jet-Long leads RULER by +4.79/+2.18/+2.03 percentage points over the strongest baseline at 1.7B/4B/8B, achieves the best overall accuracy on HELMET-RAG (a benchmark identified by HELMET as the most efficient predictor of downstream long-context performance) and attains the lowest PG-19 perplexity. Additional evaluations cover Meta-Llama-3-8B, post-trained Qwen3 checkpoints, and the hybrid Jet-Nemotron architecture, supporting broader applicability without retraining. The local-window hyperparameter remains robust across the tested settings.
